title: Beach Commons V5 — Weather School + Tide Parliament
dek: Sun, wind, rain, water, moon, fire, and stone become seven public classrooms before the whole reversible campus gathers to listen and decide
body:
Beach Commons V5 turns weather into a shared civic curriculum. The Sun Studio teaches moving shade through drawing and dance. Wind Notation Hall translates gusts into marks, weaving, gentle sound, and cooperative games. Rain Roof Choir makes a rare storm audible. Water Accounting Court asks a finite recirculated volume to serve washing, cooling, bread, plants, and play. Moon Assembly practices testimony and silence. Fire + Stone Seminar gathers food, repair, sculpture, and story around existing-style designated rings.

The closing Tide Parliament is not a government or a scientific authority. It is an imagined seasonal ritual: short public testimony, habitat reports, proposals, bread, weaving, music, sculpture, games, and votes made with ceramic tokens. Observation becomes something people do together without turning the beach into a screen, a resort, or a permanent settlement.

Eight generated plates move from the complete Weather School to the sunset assembly. The architecture remains conceptual and unpermitted. Any real version would require site-specific engineering, coastal and habitat review, accessible routes, food and fire authorization, weather limits, inland tide observation, trained stewardship, and a full removal plan.
